description: You can read a growing plant: when it's thirsty, waterlogged, frost-bitten or starved of light, and what to do about it.  Learned by tending crops.

You know how nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and pH feed a crop, how to spot which one a plant is short of, and how to feed the soil with manure, compost, ash and fertilizer without burning the roots.  Learned by fertilizing and testing soil.
You can tell blight from mildew from rot, know which diseases linger in the soil after which crops, and plan a rotation to starve them out.  Learned by dealing with sick plants.
